item1_direct_result.activation: Prefill with sglang.srt.speculative.qwen_pp4.supported() (SGLANG_QWEN_PP4_EP1=1, PP4/TP1/EP1 EAGLE3); all other layouts keep the upstream loop
mechanism: event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill_direct: a stage launches microbatch i once it is formed and its proxy arrived, then sends its proxy; no output ring and no d2h synchronize before a launch

every scheduling transition keeps an iteration index common to all stages: requests and bootstrap/transfer polls are forwarded at the start of an iteration, consensus is applied and forwarded at the same iteration on every stage, the result of the microbatch launched pp_loop_size - 1 iterations earlier is applied at the same iteration on every stage; radix inserts (EAGLE bigram keys include the first output token), allocator state and KV release therefore match

last stage: a daemon publisher thread waits on each forward's copy-stream event and sends rids, next tokens and EAGLE hidden/topk_p/topk_index (pinned host copies) to stages 0..2 on a dedicated gloo group; stages 0..2 read it at their result step and write the same aux metadata to Decode as the last stage
_QWEN_PP_CONSENSUS_LAG = 2: bootstrap and release consensus are applied two iterations after the last stage originates them (upstream pp_size - 1 = 3)
a rid assertion stops the server if stages ever formed different microbatches; a publisher failure logs and signals the parent like run_scheduler_process
item1_direct_result.not_routed: EAGLE hidden/topk never travel through NCCL; the CPU payload is ~8 KB per request

item2_proxy_transfer.path_taken: NCCL kept, moved in-stream: PyNccl ncclRecv immediately before run_batch and ncclSend immediately after it, both on the forward stream; metadata first over the PP gloo group
item2_proxy_transfer.why_not_copy_engine: cudaIpc mapping, peer stream memops or IPC events and slot back-pressure are GPU-only and cannot be exercised on CPU; Firmus policy is one serving run. In-stream NCCL reuses the P2P transfer already used by 40767107134/40796263174 and removes co-residency structurally.
item2_proxy_transfer.expected_cost: about 240 MB per microbatch per boundary is exposed on both neighbours (~1-3 ms of ~115 ms) plus waits when a neighbour is slower; a copy-engine path remains the follow-up if the profile shows this cost
